q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में फंड की कमी (low funding), इंसान-जानवर का टकराव (human-wildlife conflict), और भूमि के अधिकार (land-use rights) को चुनौती बताया गया है। "Climate change" (जलवायु परिवर्तन) का पूरे पैसेज में कोई ज़िक्र नहीं है।

t: The tone of the passage is best described as:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक ने बिना किसी व्यक्तिगत भावना (emotion) या व्यंग्य (sarcasm) के , योजना के फायदों और उसमें आने वाली बाधाओं को एक संतुलित और 'तटस्थ' (Objective) नज़रिए से पेश किया है।

p: "The idea that space and time form a four-dimensional continuum was first suggested by Hermann Minkowski as a natural consequence of Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity. In this framework, time is not an independent, absolute entity, as Newton had assumed, but rather interwoven with the three spatial dimensions into a single fabric known as space-time. Events occur at points in this space-time, and their separation is governed not by traditional Euclidean distance but by the relativistic interval, which remains invariant under changes of reference frame. This deep connection between space and time implies that the passage of time is not universal but relative: what one observer perceives as simultaneous may differ for another observer in relative motion. This concept becomes even more profound when we introduce gravity, as formulated in Einstein's General Theory of Relativity. Gravity is no longer thought of as a force in the Newtonian sense but rather as the curvature of space-time caused by the presence of mass and energy. Objects moving within this curved space-time follow geodesics—the natural paths dictated by the warping of space and time itself. This leads to the astonishing prediction that time runs differently in regions of varying gravitational potential: near a massive body, such as a black hole, time slows relative to an observer in free space. This effect, known as gravitational time dilation, has been confirmed through precise experiments, such as the observation that clocks aboard satellites tick slightly faster than those on Earth's surface due to weaker gravity."

t: Which of the following best describes the grammatical structure of the sentence: "This deep connection between space and time implies that the passage of time is not universal but relative"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: इस वाक्य में एक Main Clause ("This deep connection... implies") है और एक Dependent Clause है जो 'that' से शुरू हो रहा है ("that the passage of time is... relative")। एक Main + एक (या अधिक) Dependent Clause मिलकर Complex sentence (मिश्रित वाक्य) बनाते हैं।

t: What is the closest meaning of "geodesics" in the context of the passage?
o: Straightest possible paths in curved space-time
Circular orbits caused by gravitational pull
Fixed points of measurement in space
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज के अनुसार, 'Geodesics' वे 'प्राकृतिक रास्ते' (natural paths) हैं जो मुड़े हुए (curved) स्पेस-टाइम में कोई वस्तु अपनाती है। ज्यामिति (Geometry) में इसे मुड़े हुए स्पेस का सबसे 'सीधा रास्ता' माना जाता है। Hindi Meaning: वक्र (मुड़े हुए) स्थान-समय में सबसे सीधा रास्ता.

t: In the sentence "Gravity is no longer thought of as a force in the Newtonian sense but rather as the curvature of space-time...", what does the word "curvature" most likely refer to?
o: Bending of the path of planets only
Warping of the structure of space and time
Deformation of gravitational fields by energy
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Curvature" का अर्थ है 'झुकाव' या 'मुड़ाव' (Warping/bending)। आइंस्टीन के अनुसार गुरुत्वाकर्षण कोई बल नहीं है, बल्कि यह स्पेस-टाइम (अंतरिक्ष-समय) के फैब्रिक में भारी चीज़ों द्वारा पैदा किया गया एक झुकाव (warping) है।

p: India's startup ecosystem has witnessed remarkable growth over the past decade, transforming the country into the third-largest startup hub globally. With more than 1.5 lakh startups recognized as of early 2025, India stands out due to its vibrant entrepreneurial spirit and robust support systems. Major cities such as Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Hyderabad lead this surge, while tier-2 and tier-3 cities are increasingly contributing innovators and enterprises. The government's flagship initiative, Startup India, launched in 2016, has played a pivotal role in nurturing innovation by providing startups with financial assistance, mentorship, and regulatory ease. Additionally, a growing pool of young, tech-savvy professionals, combined with widespread internet and smartphone penetration, creates an ideal environment for digital innovations. This ecosystem has produced over a hundred unicorns, startups valued at over one billion dollars, boosting India's economic growth and employment generation substantially.

Startups are driving a cultural shift from job seekers to job creators by fostering entrepreneurial opportunities nationwide. Sectors like fintech, edtech, healthtech, and e-commerce are flourishing and addressing local challenges while gaining global recognition. The synergy among incubators, accelerators, investors, and the government continues to fuel India's ambition to become a global startup powerhouse in the years to come.

t: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence from the passage: "Startups ________ a cultural shift from job seekers to job creators by fostering entrepreneurial opportunities nationwide."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Startups' बहुवचन है और वाक्य वर्तमान में जारी बदलाव बता रहा है, इसलिए Present Continuous 'are driving' सही है।

t: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence from the passage: "This ecosystem ________ produced over a hundred unicorns, startups valued at over one billion dollars."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'ecosystem' एकवचन है और आगे 'produced' (V3) है, इसलिए Present Perfect के लिए 'has' आएगा।

t: What does the word "synergy" mean as used in the passage?
o: Cooperation that leads to a greater effect
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Synergy' का अर्थ है आपसी सहयोग जिससे अधिक प्रभाव मिले। Hindi Meaning: तालमेल / सहक्रिया.

t: The word "flourishing" in the passage most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Flourishing' का अर्थ है फलता-फूलता / तेज़ी से बढ़ता (thriving and growing)। Hindi Meaning: फलता-फूलता.

t: Which of the following best summarizes the main idea of the passage?
o: India's startup growth is mostly centered in a few large cities with little government support.
The startup ecosystem in India is shrinking due to lack of innovation.
Startups in India only focus on local markets without global ambitions.
India's startup ecosystem is expanding rapidly due to government initiatives, technology adoption, and widespread collaboration, contributing significantly to economic and employment growth.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज का मुख्य विचार: सरकारी पहलों, तकनीक और सहयोग से भारत का स्टार्टअप इकोसिस्टम तेज़ी से बढ़ रहा है और रोज़गार व अर्थव्यवस्था में योगदान दे रहा है।

p: In an economy increasingly defined by automation and volatile market dynamics, the pertinence of skill-based education has never been more conspicuous. Traditional pedagogy, with its emphasis on rote memorisation and theoretical abstraction, often fails to equip learners with the pragmatic competencies demanded by contemporary industries. This schism between academic instruction and workplace exigencies has engendered a workforce proficient in qualifications but deficient in adaptability. Skill-based education, conversely, prioritises applied learning, fostering dexterity in problem-solving, communication, and technological fluency. Apprenticeships, vocational training, and project-based curricula immerse students in authentic scenarios where knowledge is not merely recited but operationalized. Such experiential learning cultivates not only technical acumen but also critical soft skills indispensable in collaborative environments. Furthermore, skill-oriented systems encourage a mind-set of lifelong learning, essential in an era where obsolescence can render a profession archaic within a decade. They democratise opportunity by enabling individuals from diverse socio-economic backgrounds to access employment through demonstrable capability rather than academic prestige alone. Ultimately, integrating skill-based frameworks into mainstream education is not a peripheral reform but a systemic imperative. It reconciles the persistent dichotomy between learning and livelihood, ensuring that education is not an inert archive of facts but a dynamic instrument for personal agency and national progress.

t: The phrase "where knowledge is not merely recited but operationalized" functions as:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: यह क्लॉज़ 'authentic scenarios' (Noun) को डिस्क्राइब कर रहा है कि वे परिदृश्य (scenarios) कैसे हैं। Noun को मॉडिफाई करने वाला क्लॉज़ 'Adjective Clause' होता है।

t: Identify the voice in "has engendered a workforce proficient in qualifications but deficient in adaptability".
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "This schism (Subject)... has engendered (Verb)" इस वाक्य में Subject खुद काम (engender/पैदा करना) कर रहा है। यह Present Perfect Tense का Active Voice है।

t: The word "obsolescence" means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Obsolescence" का अर्थ है 'अप्रचलन' यानी किसी चीज़ (तकनीक या पेशे) का पुराना या आउटडेटेड हो जाना। Hindi Meaning: अप्रचलित हो जाना / पुराना पड़ जाना.

t: In the context of the passage, which idiom best conveys the meaning of "reconciles the persistent dichotomy between learning and livelihood"?
o: Hit the nail on the head
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Reconciles the persistent dichotomy" का अर्थ है दो अलग-अलग चीज़ों (पढ़ाई और रोज़गार) के बीच के अंतर को खत्म करना। "Bridge the gap" (खाई पाटना) इसी मुहावरे को दर्शाता है।

t: According to the passage, what is the primary advantage of skill-based education over traditional pedagogy?
o: It reduces the duration of education
It eliminates the need for academic knowledge
It bridges the gap between learning and employability
It focuses solely on manual skills
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज का मुख्य तर्क यही है कि स्किल-बेस्ड एजुकेशन थ्योरी (learning) और नौकरी (workplace exigencies/employability) के बीच के फासले (schism) को खत्म करती है।

p: The accelerating depletion of fossil fuels, coupled with mounting ecological degradation, has propelled renewable energy from a peripheral concern to a central component of global energy discourse. Yet, the conversation often fixates on production rather than application. A nuanced understanding of renewable energy must include not only its sources — solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, and biomass — but also the multifaceted domains in which it can transform economies, decentralize power structures, and promote environmental justice. In the domain of electricity generation, renewables have already begun to displace conventional energy systems. Solar photovoltaic installations now power not only urban rooftops but remote rural hamlets long excluded from centralized grids. Micro-hydel projects have enabled mountain communities to harness perennial streams for electricity without the ecological upheaval of large dams. Similarly, wind energy has emerged as a significant contributor in coastal and arid zones, transforming local economies by creating decentralized, sustainable employment ecosystems. Beyond electricity, renewable energy finds compelling applications in transportation, industrial heating, and agriculture. The rise of biofuels — especially second-generation variants derived from agricultural waste — offers a pathway to decarbonize aviation and freight transport, sectors that have traditionally been resistant to electrification. In agrarian contexts, solar-powered pumps have reduced farmers' dependence on erratic grid supply and diesel generators, enhancing irrigation autonomy while mitigating carbon emissions. Industries, often vilified for their carbon intensity, are also experimenting with renewable alternatives. Concentrated solar thermal technologies, for instance, are being employed in textile processing, food dehydration, and even metallurgy, demonstrating that clean energy need not be confined to low-intensity applications. Furthermore, geothermal energy is increasingly being harnessed for space heating in colder regions and for cooling through absorption chillers — thereby offsetting conventional HVAC loads. However, the significance of renewable energy transcends utility. At a deeper level, it challenges existing geopolitical hierarchies shaped by fossil fuel dependency. While oil-rich nations have historically wielded disproportionate influence, renewable resources — abundant yet diffuse — enable energy sovereignty for resource-scarce regions. This democratization of energy, if properly managed, can catalyze more equitable development paradigms. Nevertheless, integration challenges persist.

Intermittency, storage limitations, land use conflicts, and upfront costs are not insignificant barriers. A hasty transition without resilient infrastructure or community consent could replicate the very injustices renewables seek to redress. Therefore, the question is not merely how to produce renewable energy, but how to embed it meaningfully across sectors, geographies, and social hierarchies.

t: What primary argument does the author make about renewable energy?
o: It can only replace fossil fuels in electricity generation
It has limited potential beyond solar energy
Its transformative use lies across multiple sectors
It is primarily a Western innovation
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक का मुख्य तर्क यह है कि हमें केवल ऊर्जा 'उत्पादन' पर नहीं, बल्कि इसके कई क्षेत्रों (जैसे खेती, उद्योग, ट्रांसपोर्ट) में 'उपयोग' (multifaceted domains in which it can transform economies) पर ध्यान देना चाहिए।

t: What distinguishes second-generation biofuels, as mentioned in the passage?
o: They are made from animal fats
They derive from non-edible agricultural waste
They emit more carbon than coal
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "second-generation variants derived from agricultural waste" (वे कृषि कचरे से बनाए जाते हैं)।

t: Why is geothermal energy cited in the passage?
o: To highlight a rare and impractical solution
To exemplify its industrial cooling and heating utility
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: जिओथर्मल (भूतापीय) ऊर्जा का उदाहरण "for space heating in colder regions and for cooling" (हीटिंग और कूलिंग उपयोग) दिखाने के लिए दिया गया है।

t: According to the author, how does renewable energy challenge global power structures?
o: By enabling energy independence in diverse regions
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: अभी तक तेल वाले देशों का दबदबा (geopolitical hierarchies) था, लेकिन रिन्यूएबल ऊर्जा हर जगह पाई जाती है (diffuse), जिससे संसाधन विहीन देशों को "energy sovereignty" (ऊर्जा स्वतंत्रता) मिल सकती है।

t: What is the author's caution about the rapid adoption of renewable energy?
o: It may repeat existing patterns of injustice
It leads to fossil fuel scarcity
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक चेतावनी देता है: "A hasty transition... could replicate the very injustices r enewables seek to redress." (बिना सोचे-समझे जल्दबाज़ी करने से वही पुराने अन्याय फिर से दोहराए जा सकते हैं)।

p: In an era where urban dwellers frequently lament their paucity of time, cultivating plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles. Certain species, endowed with remarkable resilience, can subsist with negligible intervention, thereby mitigating the anxieties often concomitant with horticulture. The snake plant (Sansevieria trifasciata), for instance, is virtually indomitable. It thrives in variegated light conditions and can endure erratic watering schedules without forfeiting its structural elegance. Likewise, the pothos (Epipremnum aureum), with its luxuriant, trailing foliage, adapts to both dimly lit corners and well-illuminated spaces, performing photosynthesis with an almost stoic persistence. Another exemplar is the aloe vera, whose succulent leaves serve as reservoirs of moisture, rendering frequent irrigation superfluous. Beyond its ornamental utility, aloe vera confers medicinal benefits, its gel being esteemed for dermal amelioration. Even the ZZ plant (Zamioculcas zamiifolia), seemingly sculpted from emerald wax, flourishes in neglect, tolerating prolonged droughts and low luminosity without capitulating to decay. The allure of such flora lies not merely in their aesthetic contribution but in their implicit lesson: resilience is as captivating as fragility. In cultivating them, one engages in a quiet partnership where human oversight is ancillary, and nature's intrinsic mechanisms orchestrate survival with effortless grace.

t: "plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles." Convert the sentence into an interrogative sentence.
o: plants that demand minimal vigilance have not become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Is plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Why plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Have plants that demand minimal vigilance become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: दिया गया वाक्य Present Perfect ("have become") में है। Yes/No प्रश्न बनाने के लिए auxiliary को subject से पहले लाते हैं: "Have ... become ...?" और subject "plants that demand minimal vigilance" वैसा ही रहता है। Option (b) में "Is" (गलत tense) और (c) में "Why" (दूसरी तरह का प्रश्न) है। Trick: Have/Has + subject + V3। उत्तर (d)।

t: Rewrite the following sentence from the passage in passive voice without changing the tense: "The snake plant can endure erratic watering schedules without forfeiting its structural elegance."
o: Erratic watering schedules can be endured by the snake plant without forfeiting its structural elegance.
Erratic watering schedules are endured by the snake plant without forfeiting its structural elegance.
Erratic watering schedules will be endured by the snake plant without forfeiting its structural elegance.
Erratic watering schedules were endured by the snake plant without forfeiting its structural elegance.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Active वाक्य में "can endure" (modal + base verb) है। Modal वाले Passive का formula है: Object + modal + be + V3 + by + subject, यानी "can be endured by". Object "Erratic watering schedules" नया subject बनता है। "Are endured" में modal (क्षमता का भाव) चला जाता है और "will/were endured" में tense बदल जाता है, इसलिए ग़लत हैं। उत्तर (a)।

t: The word "capitulating" most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Capitulate" का अर्थ है विरोध छोड़कर पूरी तरह झुक जाना, यानी आत्मसमर्पण करना। ZZ plant "without capitulating to decay" पनपता है, यानी सड़न के आगे हार माने बिना। Strengthening, Multiplying और Regenerating इसके उलट बढ़ने/टिके रहने का भाव देते हैं। उत्तर (a) Surrendering। Hindi Meaning: आत्मसमर्पण करना।

t: The phrase "verdant comfort" refers to:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Verdant" का अर्थ है हरा-भरा, वनस्पति से भरपूर। "Verdant comfort" घर के भीतर हरियाली से मिलने वाले मानसिक सुकून और सुंदरता को बताता है, यानी शहरी घरों में जीवित पौधे जो शांति लाते हैं। इसलिए (c) Comfort provided by greenery सही है। Hindi Meaning: हरियाली से मिलने वाला आराम।

t: In the passage, one plant is characterised not only by its ornamental value but also by a functional benefit derived from a substance within its leaves, which is esteemed for dermal amelioration. Which plant fits this description?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में कहा गया है कि aloe vera "confers medicinal benefits, its gel being esteemed for dermal amelioration", यानी इसका gel त्वचा को सुधारने के लिए मूल्यवान माना जाता है। सजावटी और औषधीय दोनों उपयोग वर्णित पौधों में सिर्फ़ aloe vera के हैं। उत्तर (b) Aloe vera।

p: The study of literature offers profound insights into the richness of human experience, diverse cultures and complex societies. Through immersive engagement with novels, evocative poetry, compelling drama and thought-provoking essays, readers explore a wide range of emotions, intricate ethical dilemmas, social norms and historical contexts. Literature cultivates empathy by enabling individuals to comprehend varied perspectives and lived experiences beyond their own. It nurtures critical thinking, imaginative creativity and reflective analysis, empowering readers to examine human behaviour and the structures of society more deeply. Moreover, studying literature preserves invaluable cultural heritage and enduring traditions, creating meaningful connections between past and present. In educational contexts, literary study enhances advanced communication skills, sophisticated analytical abilities and nuanced moral reasoning. Engaging with carefully crafted literary texts fosters a richer understanding of humanity and its inherent complexities, shaping both individual growth and collective consciousness. By exploring the profound layers of meaning in literature, readers develop intellectual, emotional and ethical awareness that endures across a lifetime.

p: The term "enlightenment" describes a cultural milieu and intellectual movement that began in Western Europe in the seventeenth century and reached its peak in the eighteenth. Its main characteristic was the belief that human reason, universal and consistent, is adequate to solve basic issues and to set fundamental standards of living. For some Enlightenment thinkers, the model of reason was the inductive method of science, which infers universal laws from particular empirical observations. For others, particularly Descartes and his followers, reason was modeled on geometry, involving the deduction of specific truths from clear and distinct universal ideas known intuitively by the "light of reason." Many Enlightenment thinkers employed both.

t: Which of the following best describes what is meant by enlightenment?
o: An intellectual and cultural movement that originated in Western Europe
A political revolution that is mainly focused on the monarchy and governmental structures
A religious renaissance that puts faith above reason
A scientific project limited to the study of natural philosophy
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पहली पंक्ति: Enlightenment एक सांस्कृतिक व बौद्धिक आंदोलन था जो 17वीं सदी में पश्चिमी यूरोप में शुरू हुआ।

t: What was the central belief of Enlightenment thinkers?
o: Faith and tradition are superior to rational inquiry
Human reason is universal and sufficient for solving basic issues
Scientific progress depends entirely on divine intervention
Political authority should remain unquestioned and absolute
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: मुख्य विश्वास: मानव तर्क सार्वभौमिक है और बुनियादी समस्याओं को हल करने के लिए पर्याप्त है।

t: Which method did some Enlightenment thinkers use as a model for reason?
o: The intuitive approach based on religious faith
The deductive approach based on political authority
The inductive approach based on empirical observation
