p: The concept of nihilism suggests that there is no inherent meaning, value, or truth in life. It has emerged in modern times, particularly as a result of Friedrich Nietzsche's ideas about the loss of tradition,

a) religious or moral authority, and b) reason and logic, which were all once very strong in Western culture. Nihilism is mostly found in modern society, which has been experiencing rapid technological growth and an increasingly fragmented culture because of ideological fatigue and the pace of technological advancements. Nihilism produces feelings of isolation, skepticism, and apathy towards morality.

While nihilism uncovers how fragile belief systems are, it also raises the question of how one can be held responsible, have a sense of purpose, or exercise free will without a basis in something like religious, metaphysical, or logical authority. Therefore, nihilism is not only a means of negating things but also an insightful way to highlight how each of us will have to deal with the emptiness created when something we once held to be true collapses, and to evaluate the basis of what we consider important.

t: What is the main question that Nihilism asks about human existence?
o: Is having material wealth the only way to find happiness and fulfillment?
Should people reject all forms of morality and accept chaos instead?
Can technology by itself give people purpose and identity in today's world?
How can someone find meaning when traditional sources of authority are gone?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज का केंद्रीय प्रश्न: जब धार्मिक, नैतिक और तार्किक सत्ताएँ ढह जाएँ, तब मनुष्य अर्थ, उद्देश्य और ज़िम्मेदारी कैसे पाए।

t: What does the concept of Nihilism primarily suggest?
o: Life is guided by eternal moral principles
Religion is the only source of meaning in life
Life has no inherent meaning, value, or truth
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पहली पंक्ति: शून्यवाद (nihilism) मानता है कि जीवन में कोई अंतर्निहित अर्थ, मूल्य या सत्य नहीं है।

t: What modern conditions have contributed to Nihilism's spread?
o: The increased level of global integration among societies that are still heavily dedicated to their Established Values
The almost universal application of Religious and Moral Authority by a good many members of modern society
The Resurgence in the place of Logic and Metaphysics within the community
The Rapid growth in technology and a fragmented culture resulting from ideological fatigue
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: तेज़ तकनीकी विकास और वैचारिक थकान से उपजी खंडित संस्कृति ने शून्यवाद को फैलाया।

t: Why is Nihilism considered more than mere negation?
o: By denying all systems of meaning altogether, it fails to provide any kind of interpretation or analysis of life
By rejecting all systems of meaning, it encourages blind acceptance of materialism and consumerism
By insisting on strict moral guidelines to fill our lives with meaning, it is trying to fill the void of existential emptiness
By demonstrating how fragile each system of belief is, it prompts us evaluate what truly matters in life
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: यह विश्वास-प्रणालियों की नाज़ुकता दिखाकर हमें यह परखने को प्रेरित करता है कि वास्तव में क्या महत्वपूर्ण है, इसलिए यह केवल नकार नहीं है।

t: How does Nihilism usually affect people emotionally?
o: It can give a sense of empowerment and a clear idea about life's ultimate purpose.
It can make people feel more optimistic and confident in universal truths.
Stronger commitment to religious and ethical traditions.
It can lead to feelings of isolation, skepticism, and not caring much about morality.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: शून्यवाद अकेलेपन, संशयवाद और नैतिकता के प्रति उदासीनता (apathy) की भावनाएँ पैदा करता है।

p: India's tryst with chess is deeply interwoven with its cultural heritage, for the game itself originally known as "chaturanga" emerged on the subcontinent over a millennium ago. Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare, "chaturanga" evolved into shatranj under Persian influence before migrating westward, ultimately becoming modern chess. In the contemporary era, India's prominence on the global chess stage began with the meteoric ascent of Viswanathan Anand in the late 20th century. Anand's fluid playing style, amalgamating tactical precision with positional depth, earned him the World Chess Championship title multiple times and inspired a generation of players. His success catalysed institutional investment in chess, leading to an upsurge in tournaments, academies, and grassroots initiatives across the country. The 21st century has witnessed the emergence of prodigies such as Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa, D. Gukesh, and Nihal Sarin, whose exploits in international arenas have positioned India as a formidable force in team events like the Chess Olympiad. Digital platforms have further accelerated talent development, enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide, thus refining their strategic acumen from an early age. Today, India stands not merely as the cradle of chess's origins but as an influential power shaping its future. This continuity from ancient invention to modern innovation underscores the nation's enduring legacy in the chess world.

t: The phrase "enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters" functions as:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: यह फ्रेज़ Present Participle (V1+ing) "enabling" से शुरू होता है और पूरे क्लॉज़ के परिणाम को बताता है। जो फ्रेज़ Participle से शुरू हो, उसे 'Participle Phrase' कहते हैं।

t: Identify the voice in "Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare".
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Conceived" (V3) का इस्तेमाल यहाँ पैसिव सेंस में हुआ है। चतुरंग को 'बनाया गया था' (It was conceived)। एजेंट (बनाने वाला) गायब है।

t: The word "meteoric" most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Meteoric ascent" (उल्कापिंड जैसी उड़ान) का मतलब है ऐसी तरक्की जो बहुत ही 'तेज़ और शानदार' (rapid and spectacular) हो। Hindi Meaning: रातोंरात / बहुत तेज़ तरक्की.

t: The word "acumen" means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Strategic acumen" का मतलब है कू टनीतिक 'कुशाग्रता' या 'तेज़ समझ' (Sharpness in understanding / mental keenness)। Hindi Meaning: कुशाग्रता / बुद्धिमत्ता.

t: According to the passage, what factor in recent years has accelerated chess talent development in India?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज कहता है: "Digital platforms have further accelerated talent development, enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide."

p: The annals of mountaineering history are adorned with figures whose daring transcended mere athleticism, embodying philosophical quests for transcendence against Earth's most formidable landscapes. Each mountaineer whether treading the snows of Everest, the granite of Patagonia, or the arid heights of the Atlas Mountains - etched a distinct narrative of audacity and introspection. "Tenzing Norgay" and "Sir Edmund Hillary's" epochal 1953 Everest ascent immortalized human perseverance, but figures such as "Reinhold Messner" redefined the boundaries further. Rejecting supplemental oxygen, Messner's minimalist ethos emphasized purity over conquest, portraying mountains not as trophies but as sentient entities commanding reverence. Similarly, "Junko Tabei", the first woman to summit Everest, symbolized the intersection of resilience and quiet defiance in an era resistant to female adventurers. The ethos of mountaineering diversified through the late 20th and early 21st centuries. Climbers like "Kilian Jornet", blending ultra-marathon endurance with technical ascents, and "Nirmal Purja", whose record-breaking summits shattered temporal assumptions, reveal a contemporary paradigm: mountains as arenas of rapid, almost transcendental athleticism. Meanwhile, indigenous climbers, long relegated to footnotes in expedition histories, increasingly assert their rightful place as stewards of sacred peaks. Thus, the saga of mountaineering resists reduction to mere feats of strength. It weaves a tapestry of cultures, philosophies, and personal odysseys each ascent a dialectic between human fragility and the immutable majesty of the mountains.

t: In the sentence: "The annals of mountaineering history are adorned with figures whose daring transcended mere athleticism..."? What is the grammatical role of the clause "whose daring transcended mere athleticism"
o: Noun clause acting as the subject
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Whose" एक Relative Pronoun है जो अपने से ठीक पहले आए Noun "figures" की विशेषता बता रहा है। संज्ञा (Noun) को मॉडिफाई करने वाले क्लॉज़ को Adjective Clause कहते हैं।

t: What is the meaning of the word "epochal" in the context: "Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary's epochal 1953 Everest ascent..."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Epochal" (युगांतरकारी) का अर्थ है कोई ऐसी घटना जो इतनी महत्वपूर्ण हो कि वह एक नए युग (epoch) की शुरुआत कर दे। Hindi Meaning: युगांतरकारी / ऐतिहासिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण.

t: What does the word "dialectic" most nearly imply in the phrase: "...each ascent a dialectic between human fragility and the immutable majesty of the mountains"?
o: A dialogue or interplay between opposing forces
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Dialectic" का उपयोग यहाँ रूपक (metaphor) के रूप में हुआ है। यह इंसान की कमज़ोरी (fragility) और पहाड़ की अपार ताकत (majesty) जैसे दो विरोधी बलों (opposing forces) के बीच के तनाव या खेल को दर्शाता है।

t: Which of the following best summarizes the primary argument of the passage?
o: Mountaineering is solely a test of physical endurance.
Mountaineering history is dominated by Western adventurers.
Mountaineering represents a confluence of physical challenge, cultural identity, and philosophical exploration.
Technological advancements have made mountaineering effortless.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज बार-बार कहता है कि पर्वतारोहण केवल शारीरिक ताकत का खेल नहीं है, बल्कि यह एक "tapestry of cultures, philosophies, and personal odysseys" (शारीरिक, सांस्कृतिक और दार्शनिक अन्वेषण का संगम) है।

t: Which word could best replace "immutable" in the phrase "...the immutable majesty of the mountains..." without significantly changing the meaning?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Immutable" का अर्थ होता है 'अपरिवर्तनीय' (जिसमें कभी कोई बदलाव न हो)। पहाड़ों की महानता हमेशा स्थायी रहती है। "Unchanging" इसका सटीक समानार्थी है।

p: The metamorphosis of a butterfly epitomizes one of nature's most intricate and captivating transformations. The life cycle initiates with the deposition of fragile eggs, often hidden on the underside of leaves, ensuring immediate access to nourishment upon hatching. Once emerged, the larva — or caterpillar — enters a phase of relentless consumption, devouring foliage to fuel its rapid growth. During this stage, it undergoes multiple molts, shedding its rigid exoskeleton to accommodate its expanding form. This insatiable feeding period is essential for amassing the energy required for the subsequent, dramatic metamorphosis. The transition into the pupal stage, encapsulated within a chrysalis, marks an extraordinary biological phenomenon. Inside, the caterpillar's structures are enzymatically dismantled and reconstructed into entirely new forms — wings, antennae, and compound eyes emerge through a sophisticated process known as histogenesis. Upon completing this hidden transformation, the adult butterfly struggles free, its crumpled wings needing to be inflated with hemolymph and dried before flight is possible. Once airborne, the butterfly's existence centres on reproduction, perpetuating the species before its ephemeral life concludes. Though often romanticized, the butterfly's life cycle underscores a rigorous narrative of survival, adaptation, and evolutionary precision, offering profound insights into the fragile balance of ecosystems.

t: Identify the sentence from the passage which is in the passive voice:
o: "The metamorphosis of a butterfly epitomizes transformation."
"The butterfly inflates its wings with hemolymph."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: इस वाक्य में "are... dismantled" (Be-verb + Past Participle V3) का प्रयोग हुआ है, जो ष्ट रूप से Passive Voice की पहचान है। यहाँ Subject (structures) स्प पर काम किया जा रहा है।

t: Which sentence contains a relative clause?
o: "Its crumpled wings need to be inflated."
"Eggs are often hidden on the underside of leaves."
"A caterpillar devours foliage to fuel its growth."
"The larva, which undergoes multiple molts, grows rapidly."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "which undergoes multiple molts" एक Relative Clause है जो Relative Pronoun "which" से शुरू होता है और 'larva' के बारे में अतिरिक्त जानकारी देता है।

t: Which word from the passage is derived by adding a Greek-origin suffix meaning "formation" or "origin"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: ग्रीक सफिक्स (Suffix) "-genesis" का अर्थ होता है "निर्माण, रचना या उत्पत्ति" (creation/formation)। "Histo" का अर्थ है ऊतक (tissue), इसलिए 'Histogenesis' का अर्थ ऊतकों का निर्माण है।

t: According to the passage, what crucial biological activity occurs within the chrysalis?
o: Rebuilding of the caterpillar into a butterfly through histogenesis
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में साफ़ लिखा है कि chrysalis (कोकून) के अंदर कैटरपिलर का ढांचा एंजाइम्स द्वारा तोड़ा जाता है और "reconstructed into entirely new forms... known as histogenesis."

t: In the passage, the word "ephemeral" most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Ephemeral" का अर्थ होता है 'क्षणिक' या बहुत कम समय तक जीवित रहने वाला। "Transient" (अस्थायी/क्षणिक) इसका सटीक समानार्थी (Synonym) है। "Everlasting" इसका विलोम (Antonym) है। Hindi Meaning: क्षणिक / अल्पकालिक.

p: Human decision-making is rarely based on logic alone; emotion, bias, and perception play critical roles, especially in assessing risk. Psychologists have observed that people often fear unlikely events—such as airplane crashes—more than common dangers like car accidents. This "availability heuristic" leads individuals to judge risks based on how easily examples come to mind, not on actual probability. Moreover, emotions like fear or excitement can distort rational thinking. People also tend to avoid losses more strongly than they pursue gains, a concept known as "loss aversion." This is why investors might hold on to failing stocks rather than accept a small loss. Understanding these psychological patterns can improve personal and policy-level decisions. Rather than eliminating emotion, effective risk management involves recognizing how it influences choices. Awareness of these tendencies allows individuals to make more balanced, informed decisions in uncertain situations.

t: A passage is given with five questions following it. Read the passage carefully and select the best answer to each question out of the given four alternatives:
What is the availability heuristic, as described in the passage?
o: Estimating risk by logic and data
Judging risk based on memorable examples
q.e: According to the passage, the "availability heuristic" is a psychological pattern where individuals judge the likelihood of risks based on how easily specific examples come to mind. This often leads people to fear dramatic but rare events, like airplane crashes, because they are more memorable.

t: Which of the following best illustrates loss aversion?
o: Donating to charity instead of investing
Accepting minor setbacks to avoid stress
Holding on to a losing stock to avoid admitting loss
q.e: The passage defines "loss aversion" as the tendency to avoid losses more strongly than pursuing gains, giving the specific example of investors holding on to failing stocks. Option C directly reflects this example provided in the text to illustrate the psychological concept.

t: According to the passage,why do people often misjudge rare events as more dangerous?
o: Because they consult experts too much
Because these events are vividly remembered
Because they lack access to media
q.e: The passage explains the "availability heuristic," where people judge risks based on how easily examples come to mind. Rare but vivid events like airplane crashes are more easily remembered than common dangers, leading to a misjudgment of their actual probability.

t: What is the author's main suggestion regarding emotion in decision-making?
o: It must be ignored in financial matters
It should be recognized and managed
q.e: The author concludes that rather than eliminating emotion, effective risk management involves recognizing how it influences choices. Awareness of these tendencies allows individuals to make more balanced and informed decisions in uncertain situations, supporting the idea of management over elimination.

t: What is the overall purpose of the passage?
o: To promote emotional choices over data
To explain psychological biases in risk decisions
q.e: The passage discusses various psychological factors like the availability heuristic and loss aversion that affect human decision-making and risk assessment. Its primary goal is to explain these biases and suggest that recognizing them leads to better, more informed choices.

p: The idea of progress has always gone hand in hand with the evolution of human beings and the invention of technology. Each technological revolution has unearthed revolutionary changes that have rewritten the human experience in the past. From the invention of the printing press to the invention of the internet, technological breakthroughs have shaped the manner in which we live, work, and communicate. But with our arrival in an age of artificial intelligence, automation, and biotechnology comes a growing paradox: while these technologies offer unparalleled convenience and power, they also undermine tried-and-true social forms and erode the very notion of what it means to be human. Technological advances, first of all, have provided standards of living much better. Medical advances like gene editing and precision medicine hold the promise to cure diseases that were once thought incurable. Communication technology has made the world think alike in ways that people could not have imagined a couple of decades ago, with people able to work together across borders and cultures with relative ease. But the same technology has profound implications. Automation is taking away jobs for millions of people, particularly where human labor can be automated. The speed of innovation has left millions behind, and with it there is a feeling of disconnection, fear for the future. Secondly, our dependence on technology is creating basic questions regarding privacy, security, and freedom. As we introduce AI into everyday life, do we have to sit back and ask ourselves: are we Master of Technology, or is technology the master of us? The paradox of progress, then, is in its double-edged nature. On one hand, technology comes bearing answers to some of humankind's biggest problems, yet it also brings new issues that human beings must resolve in order to make progress mean a more just and sustainable tomorrow.

t: What is the main paradox introduced in the passage regarding technological advancements?
o: Technology always improves the quality of life
Technology eliminates all forms of labor
Technology offers convenience but also undermines social structures and the notion of being human
Technology solves all human problems without consequences
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: विरोधाभास (Paradox) यह है कि तकनीक सुविधा (convenience) तो देती है, लेकिन इंसानियत की पहचान और सामाजिक ढांचों को नुकसान (undermine) भी पहुँचाती है।

t: According to the passage, what has been one of the positive impacts of technological advances?
o: Medical advances such as gene editing and precision medicine promise to cure previously incurable diseases
Communication technology has caused more isolation
Technological advances have had no impact on the standard of living
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सकारात्मक प्रभाव (positive impact) के तौर पर पैसेज में "gene editing and precision medicine" का ज़िक्र है जो लाइलाज बीमारियों को ठीक कर सकते हैं।

t: What negative consequence of technology is mentioned in the passage?
o: It creates a sense of disconnection and fear for the future
It helps people across borders and cultures
It eliminates the need for privacy
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज कहता है कि तेज़ इनोवेशन के कारण लाखों लोग पीछे छूट गए हैं, जिससे "a feeling of disconnection, fear for the future" (अलगाव और भविष्य का डर) पैदा हो गया है।

t: What question does the passage raise about our relationship with technology?
o: How can we make technology more affordable?
How can we use technology to solve political conflicts?
Are we masters of technology, or is technology the master of us?
Should we stop using technology altogether?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज सीधे यह दार्शनिक सवाल उठाता है: "are we Master of Technology, or is technology the master of us?" (क्या हम तकनीक के मालिक हैं, या तकनीक हमारी मालिक है?)।

t: What does the passage suggest is necessary to make progress more just and sustainable?
o: Resolving the new issues brought by technology
Relying solely on automation to solve problems
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: प्रगति को न्यायसंगत (just) और टिकाऊ (sustainable) बनाने के लिए, हमें "new issues that human beings must resolve" (तकनीक द्वारा पैदा किए गए नए मुद्दों को हल करना होगा)।

p: Bertolt Brecht began writing plays in the 1920s, but they didn't gain recognition in the West until the mid-20th century, when people began rejecting Stanislavsky-oriented realism and the presentation of Well-made plays on stage. Epic theatre is based on the theories and practices developed by Brecht in the twenties. 'Epic theatre, German episches Theatre, a mode of instructive theatre showing a number of not so tightly knit scenes that refrained from creating an illusion and frequently broke the plot to talk to the spectators in a direct manner with analysis, argument, or evidence.' It follows the episodic structure and didactic style of Expressionist drama directed by Erwin Piscator. In these plays, Brecht makes use of 'alienation effect' to dissuade the audience from empathizing with characters and focus objectively on the action and argument and draw a conclusion. This theatre also shows Chinese theatre influence, as the actors kept a distance from the characters they impersonated on stage.

t: Why did Brecht's plays gain recognition in the West only in the mid-20th century?
o: The audiences started to reject the realism of Stanislavsky and the well-made plays and looked for new theatrical forms.
Brecht changed his style and began writing romantic dramas, which were easier to digest by the public.
An explanation for this is that his plays were not allowed in Europe until the end of World War II.
Another reason for this is that he deserted political matters and solely concentrated on entertainment.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: ब्रेख़्त के नाटकों को मान्यता तब मिली जब लोग स्टैनिस्लावस्की के यथार्थवाद और well-made plays को नकारकर नए रंगमंच की ओर मुड़े।

t: What is the defining feature of Epic Theatre according to Brecht's theory?
o: A plot that is closely woven together and thus conjures up a strong illusion of reality along with emotional identification
An emphasis on melodrama and sentimental storytelling in order to evoke empathy
A series of loosely connected scenes that break the illusion and encourage critical thinking
The use of improvisation as the only means of communication without any structured narrative
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: एपिक थिएटर की पहचान: ढीले जुड़े दृश्य जो भ्रम (illusion) तोड़ते हैं और दर्शकों को आलोचनात्मक सोच के लिए प्रेरित करते हैं।

t: Which theatrical technique did Brecht use to prevent audience empathy and maintain critical distance?
o: Alienation effect, keeps the audience critical
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: ब्रेख़्त ने दर्शकों को सहानुभूति से रोकने और तटस्थ रखने के लिए 'alienation effect' का प्रयोग किया।

t: What was the factor that contributed to Brecht's concept that performers ought to maintain a certain amount of detachment from their roles?
o: The spontaneous methods used in the Italian commedia dell'arte
The movements of the Chinese theatre, where players do not completely identify with their character
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: चीनी रंगमंच का प्रभाव, जहाँ अभिनेता निभाए जा रहे पात्र से दूरी बनाए रखते थे।

t: Which of the following best distinguishes Epic Theatre from traditional realist drama?
o: It presents the story in an episodic manner and interacts with the audience directly to provoke their critical thinking
It seeks to encourage the audience's emotional release by making the illusion of reality more convincing.
It avoids addressing social issues and primarily explores internal psychological conflicts.
It emphasizes ornate sets and costumes specifically to heighten the illusion of reality.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: एपिक थिएटर कथा को खंडों (episodic) में दिखाता है और दर्शकों से सीधे संवाद कर उनकी आलोचनात्मक सोच जगाता है, जबकि यथार्थवादी नाटक भ्रम को गहरा करता है।

t: Why did Brecht's plays gain recognition in the West only in the mid-20th century?
o: The audiences started to reject the realism of Stanislavsky and the well-made plays and looked for new theatrical forms.
Brecht changed his style and began writing romantic dramas, which were easier to digest by the public.
An explanation for this is that his plays were not allowed in Europe until the end of World War II.
Another reason for this is that he deserted political matters and solely concentrated on entertainment.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: लोगों के यथार्थवाद और well-made plays को अस्वीकार करने पर ही ब्रेख़्त को पश्चिम में मान्यता मिली।

t: What is the defining feature of Epic Theatre according to Brecht's theory?
o: A plot that is closely woven together and thus conjures up a strong illusion of reality along with emotional identification
An emphasis on melodrama and sentimental storytelling in order to evoke empathy
A series of loosely connected scenes that break the illusion and encourage critical thinking
The use of improvisation as the only means of communication without any structured narrative
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: एपिक थिएटर: ढीले जुड़े दृश्य जो भ्रम तोड़कर आलोचनात्मक चिंतन बढ़ाते हैं।

t: Which theatrical technique did Brecht use to prevent audience empathy and maintain critical distance?
o: Alienation effect, keeps the audience critical
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सहानुभूति रोकने और आलोचनात्मक दूरी रखने के लिए alienation effect प्रयुक्त हुआ।

t: What was the factor that contributed to Brecht's concept that performers ought to maintain a certain amount of detachment from their roles?
o: The spontaneous methods used in the Italian commedia dell'arte
The movements of the Chinese theatre, where players do not completely identify with their character
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: अभिनेताओं में पात्र से अलगाव की प्रेरणा चीनी रंगमंच की शैली से आई।

t: Which of the following best distinguishes Epic Theatre from traditional realist drama?
o: It presents the story in an episodic manner and interacts with the audience directly to provoke their critical thinking
It seeks to encourage the audience's emotional release by making the illusion of reality more convincing.
It avoids addressing social issues and primarily explores internal psychological conflicts.
It emphasizes ornate sets and costumes specifically to heighten the illusion of reality.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: एपिक थिएटर कथा को खंडों में दिखाकर और दर्शकों से सीधे बात कर उनकी आलोचनात्मक सोच जगाता है।

p: The debate over whether working from home is better than working from the office has intensified, especially after the global shift during the pandemic. While remote work offers flexibility and saves commuting time, many experts argue that office work remains more effective for several reasons. Offices provide a structured environment where employees can separate personal and professional lives. Face-to-face interactions promote quick problem-solving, spontaneous discussions, and stronger teamwork — elements often difficult to replicate virtually. Being in an office also helps maintain discipline and reduces distractions common at home, such as chores or family interruptions. Another important factor is the psychological impact. For many, the daily routine of getting ready, commuting, and working with colleagues boosts motivation and creates a sense of belonging. It also helps prevent the isolation that remote workers sometimes experience. While technology enables virtual collaboration, human connection and workplace culture often thrive better in physical spaces. In-person environments support relationship-building and allow managers to observe and support employees more effectively. Therefore, while remote work has advantages like flexibility and comfort, the traditional office still plays a key role in productivity, mental well-being, and professional development. A balanced approach, blending remote and in-office work might offer the best of both worlds, catering to different needs while preserving efficiency and connection.

t: In the sentence: "While remote work offers flexibility and saves commuting time, many experts argue that working from the office remains more effective for several reasons." What is the part of speech of the word "flexibility"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Flexibility" (लचीलापन) वाक्य में "offers" क्रिया (verb) का Direct Object है। किसी भी भाव, गुण, व्यक्ति या वस्तु के नाम को Noun (संज्ञा) कहते हैं। जिन शब्दों के अंत में '-ity' लगा होता है, वे प्रायः Abstract Nouns होते हैं।

t: In the sentence: "Another important factor is the psychological impact." What type of adjective is the word "psychological"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Psychological" (मनोवैज्ञानिक) शब्द "impact" (Noun) की प्रकृति या विशेषता (quality) का वर्णन कर रहा है। ऐसे विशेषण जो किसी नाउन के रंग, रूप, आकार या गुण का वर्णन करते हैं, उन्हें 'Descriptive Adjective' (गुणवाचक विशेषण) कहा जाता है।

t: Which of the following word pairs is a correct collocation found in the passage?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Collocation उन शब्दों का समूह होता है जो स्वाभाविक रूप से एक साथ इस्तेमाल होते हैं। पैसेज में स्पष्ट रूप से "boosts motivation" (प्रेरणा बढ़ाता है) का प्रयोग किया गया है।

t: Face-to-face interactions promote ___ problem-solving and stronger teamwork.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में साफ़ लिखा है: "Face-to-face interactions promote quick problem-solving..." (आमने-सामने की बातचीत से समस्याओं का 'त्वरित' यानी जल्दी समाधान होता है)।

t: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Remote work is always better than office work
Working from home is perfect for everyone
Working in an office has clear advantages over working from home
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: हालाँकि पैसेज वर्क -फ्रॉम-होम के कुछ फायदे बताता है, लेकिन यह लगातार ऑफिस के स्ट्रक्चरल, मनोवैज्ञानिक और सहयोगात्मक फायदों पर ज़ोर देता है (जैसे अनुशासन, टीमवर्क , एकांत से बचना)। इसलिए मुख्य विचार यही है कि ऑफिस में काम करने के स्पष्ट फायदे हैं।

p: Jack Finney's fascinating story, The Third Level, follows Charley, an ordinary thirty-one-year-old clerk who unexpectedly discovers a portal to the past within Grand Central Station. Hurrying home to his wife, Louisa, on a hot summer evening, Charley takes a wrong turn down an unfamiliar, sloping subterranean corridor. Instead of returning to the standard platforms, he emerges onto a mysterious third level. Here, the room is visibly smaller, dim open-flame gaslights flicker, and commuters are dressed in late-nineteenth-century attire. Factual verification occurs when he notices an 1894 edition of The World newspaper that reports on President Cleveland. Seeking a peaceful escape from the intense insecurities, anxieties, and stresses of modern life, Charley attempts to buy two railway tickets to Galesburg, Illinois. However, the ticket clerk rejects his modern currency, warning him that it is not legal tender. Although Charley escapes arrest and later buys vintage bills, he can never locate the entrance to the elusive third level again.

t: According to the passage, how does Charley confirm that he has arrived in the year 1894?
o: He compares his modern wristwatch with the old wooden clock in the station.
He reads an old edition of The World newspaper covering President Cleveland.
He seeks the advice of a local coin dealer on the premium value of old bills.
He meets his wife, Louisa, who tells him the history of the building.
q.e: The passage explicitly states that factual verification occurs for Charley exactly "when he notices an 1894 edition of The World newspaper that reports on President Cleveland."

t: What can be inferred about the world Charley discovered on the third level?
o: It was a busy industrial area going through rapid urban growth.
It was a very dangerous place where outsiders were arrested right away.
It was a simpler, more tranquil era compared to the modern day.
It was a modern terminal with electric lighting.
q.e: The text notes that Charley seeks a "peaceful escape" from intense modern stresses by going to Galesburg in 1894. This highly implies that the historical era he discovered on the third level was perceived as much simpler, safer, and remarkably tranquil.

t: Based on the passage, why did Charley's attempt to buy train tickets to Galesburg fail?
o: The railway platforms leading to Illinois had been permanently demolished.
The ticket clerk was highly suspicious of his late-nineteenth-century attire.
The station had run out of vintage bills required to issue transit vouchers.
His currency was not recognized as valid by the station's ticket clerk.
q.e: The passage clearly details the failure of his transaction, stating that "the ticket clerk rejects his modern currency, warning him that it is not legal tender" in that specific historical time period.

t: In the first paragraph, the word "subterranean" is used. Which of the following words best defines "subterranean" as used in the context of the story?
q.e: The English adjective "subterranean" strictly originates from Latin ("sub" meaning under, and "terra" meaning earth). It flawlessly defines something existing, occurring, or situated completely under the earth's surface, like a deep underground railway corridor.

p: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (2014): The fast urbanization of Indian cities has led to the problem of waste disposal becoming a major concern. The latest data indicate that waste collection is at 68%, but the treatment stage is only 28%. The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was initiated to tackle issues in waste management, hygiene, and sanitation at the national level in 2014.

This scheme brings along new and better waste collection systems, more sophisticated sorting and recycling methods, and full support of the concepts of reducing, reusing, and recycling. The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, through community participation and better sanitation, aspires to cut down waste in the landfills and, consequently, also the negative impact on nature. The project also insists on the necessity of proper waste handling and treatment. The aspect of public awareness is vital in the project, since it is through this that people get to be informed about eco-friendly practices. The construction of toilets in millions has greatly reduced the incidence of open defecation and the health issues associated with it. Local bodies have also experimented with waste management techniques, thus contributing to the country being cleaner and more civilized.

t: The passage indicates that the primary objective of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was to:
o: Provide technological upgrades to industries that specialize in commercial recycling systems
Promote the development of large-scale waste-to-energy facilities in major metropolitan regions.
Enhance tourism by improving the aesthetics of public spaces without addressing sanitation concerns.
Address the increasing challenge of waste disposal resulting from rapid urbanization in Indian cities.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: तेज़ शहरीकरण से अपशिष्ट निपटान बड़ी समस्या बना और इसी से निपटने के लिए 2014 में स्वच्छ भारत अभियान शुरू हुआ।

t: According to the passage, one of the key strengths of the Abhiyan is its emphasis on:
o: Replacing all existing municipal systems with privately managed services.
Investing heavily in advanced machinery at the cost of public involvement.
Enforcing strict penalties on households generating large quantities of solid waste.
Encouraging community participation and widespread public awareness.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज के अनुसार अभियान की प्रमुख ताकत सामुदायिक भागीदारी और व्यापक जन-जागरूकता है।

t: The passage indicates that Abhiyan's contribution to sanitation is most clearly seen in:
o: The privatization of rural water systems for better efficiency.
The introduction of imported sanitation technology for urban households.
A significant expansion of sewage treatment plants in industrial zones.
The construction of millions of toilets that reduced open defecation.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लाखों शौचालयों के निर्माण से खुले में शौच और उससे जुड़ी स्वास्थ्य समस्याएँ घटीं; यही स्वच्छता में अभियान का स्पष्ट योगदान है।

t: Which of the following best describes the environmental goal of the Abhiyan?
o: Expanding landfill space to handle more waste.
Encouraging citizens to rely solely on biodegradable materials for daily use.
Getting rid of all plastic waste by banning it nationwide.
Reducing waste sent to landfills by improving collection, treatment, and recycling.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: अभियान का पर्यावरणीय लक्ष्य बेहतर संग्रह, उपचार और रीसाइक्लिंग से लैंडफिल में जाने वाला कचरा घटाना है।

t: The reference to local bodies experimenting with waste management suggests that:
o: Innovative sanitation techniques were not taken up by the the municipal authorities.
Waste management was completely handed over to private companies.
Experimental methods were applied without much consideration of public opinion, replacing traditional systems.
Local governments were instrumental in the formation of cleaner and tidier communities.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: स्थानीय निकायों के प्रयोगों से देश अधिक स्वच्छ और सभ्य बना, यानी स्थानीय सरकारों की इसमें अहम भूमिका रही।

p: The metamorphosis of a butterfly epitomizes one of nature's most intricate and captivating transformations. The life cycle initiates with the deposition of fragile eggs, often hidden on the underside of leaves, ensuring immediate access to nourishment upon hatching. Once emerged, the larva or caterpillar enters a phase of relentless consumption, devouring foliage to fuel its rapid growth. During this stage, it undergoes multiple molts, shedding its rigid exoskeleton to accommodate its expanding form. This insatiable feeding period is essential for amassing the energy required for the subsequent, dramatic metamorphosis. The transition into the pupal stage, encapsulated within a chrysalis, marks an extraordinary biological phenomenon. Inside, the caterpillar's structures are enzymatically dismantled and reconstructed into entirely new forms wings, antennae, and compound eyes emerge through a sophisticated process known as histogenesis. Upon completing this hidden transformation, the adult butterfly struggles free, its crumpled wings needing to be inflated with hemolymph and dried before flight is possible. Once airborne, the butterfly's existence centres on reproduction, perpetuating the species before its ephemeral life concludes. Though often romanticized, the butterfly's life cycle underscores a rigorous narrative of survival, adaptation, and evolutionary precision, offering profound insights into the fragile balance of ecosystems.

t: Identify the sentence from the passage which is in the passive voice:
o: "The metamorphosis of a butterfly epitomizes transformation."
"The butterfly inflates its wings with hemolymph."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य में "are... dismantled" (Be-verb + Past Participle) का प्रयोग हुआ है, जो स्पष्ट रूप से Passive Voice (कर्मवाच्य) की पहचान है।

t: Which sentence contains a relative clause?
o: "Its crumpled wings need to be inflated."
"Eggs are often hidden on the underside of leaves."
"A caterpillar devours foliage to fuel its growth."
"The larva, which undergoes multiple molts, grows rapidly."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: इस वाक्य में "which undergoes multiple molts" एक Relative Clause है जो Relative Pronoun "which" से शुरू हो रहा है और 'larva' (संज्ञा) की विशेषता बता रहा है।

t: Which word from the passage is derived by adding a Greek-origin suffix meaning "formation" or "origin"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: ग्रीक सफिक्स (Suffix) "-genesis" का अर्थ होता है "निर्माण, रचना या उत्पत्ति" (creation/formation)। जीव विज्ञान में 'Histogenesis' का अर्थ ऊतकों (tissues) का निर्माण है।

t: According to the passage, what crucial biological activity occurs within the chrysalis?
o: Rebuilding of the caterpillar into a butterfly through histogenesis
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में साफ़ लिखा है कि chrysalis (कोकून) के अंदर कैटरपिलर का ढांचा टूटता है और "reconstructed into entirely new forms... known as histogenesis."

t: In the passage, the word "ephemeral" most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Ephemeral" का अर्थ होता है 'क्षणिक' या बहुत कम समय तक जीवित रहने वाला। "Transient" (अस्थायी/क्षणिक) इसका सटीक समानार्थी (Synonym) है। Hindi Meaning: क्षणिक / अल्पकालिक.

p: In the age of endless options-from streaming services to social media platforms-modern individuals face what psychologists call "decision fatigue." Unlike earlier generations who had limited choices, today's youth are constantly required to decide: what to watch, whom to follow, what to share, and how to respond. While freedom of choice is often celebrated, too many choices can lead to stress, dissatisfaction, and even paralysis. Ironically, abundance can become overwhelming. Algorithms, designed to predict preferences, often narrow exposure rather than broaden it, creating digital bubbles. People may feel in control, yet their choices are subtly shaped by unseen patterns. Over time, the constant need to choose can drain mental energy, leaving individuals anxious or indifferent. True digital freedom may lie not in limitless options, but in mindful engagement and setting personal boundaries. Recognising when to choose-and when to step back-could be the new wisdom of the connected age.

t: What is the main issue discussed in the passage?
o: Stress caused by excessive digital choices
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज की पहली ही लाइन में "decision fatigue" (निर्णय लेने की थकान) का ज़िक्र है, जो बहुत ज़्यादा विकल्पों (endless options) के कारण होने वाले तनाव को दर्शाता है।

t: What does the author imply about algorithms?
o: They limit exposure to diverse content
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज कहता है कि एल्गोरिदम "narrow exposure rather than broaden it, creating digital bubbles." (वे हमारी सोच का दायरा बढ़ाने के बजाय उसे सिकोड़ देते हैं और हमें एक 'बुलबुले' में कैद कर देते हैं)।

t: What paradox is presented in the passage?
o: Choice leads to control but also exhaustion
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: विरोधाभास (Paradox) यह है कि जहाँ चुनाव की आज़ादी (freedom of choice) को अच्छा माना जाता है , वहीं बहुत ज़्यादा विकल्प हमें मानसिक रूप से थका (drain mental energy / exhaustion) देते हैं।

t: According to the author, what may be a solution?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: समाधान के तौर पर लेखक कहता है: "mindful engagement and setting personal boundaries." (यानी सोच-समझकर इस्तेमाल करना और अपनी सीमाएं तय करना)।

t: What is the tone of the passage?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक हमें इस "निर्णय की थकान" (decision fatigue) के प्रति 'चेतावनी' (caution) दे रहा है और डिजिटल दुनिया के सही इस्तेमाल पर 'विचार' (reflect) कर रहा है।

p: In today's fast paced world, maintaining a nutritious diet has become increasingly challenging for youngsters. Surrounded by fast food outlets and sugary snacks, many adolescents are tempted to choose convenience over nourishment. However, health experts emphasize that cultivating healthy eating habits during youth is vital for long-term well-being. A balanced diet, rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins, can significantly boost immunity, enhance concentration, and prevent lifestyle diseases such as obesity and diabetes. Additionally, developing mindful eating practices helps youngsters make conscious choices about what they consume, rather than eating impulsively. Therefore, parents and schools play a pivotal role in promoting a healthy lifestyle by providing access to nutritious meals and educating young people about the consequences of poor dietary choices. If youngsters adopt healthy eating patterns early, they are more likely to carry these habits into adulthood, reaping lifelong benefits.

t: Identify the tense of the verb "has become" in the first sentence.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Has + V3 (become) का प्रयोग हमेशा Present Perfect Tense में होता है।

t: Choose the option that correctly changes this sentence into passive voice: "Parents and schools play a pivotal role in promoting a healthy lifestyle."
o: A pivotal role is played by parents and schools in promoting a healthy lifestyle.
Parents and schools are played by a pivotal role in promoting a healthy lifestyle.
A pivotal role was played by parents and schools in promoting a healthy lifestyle.
A pivotal role is play by parents and schools for promoting a healthy lifestyle.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य Simple Present Tense (play) में है। पैसिव का रूल is/are/am + V3 होता है। 'A pivotal role' (Object) Subject बन जाएगा और 'is played' का प्रयोग होगा।

t: What does "cultivating" most nearly mean as used in the passage?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Cultivating healthy eating habits" का मतलब है अच्छी आदतों को 'विकसित करना' या अपनाना (Developing)। Hindi Meaning: विकसित करना / पैदा करना.

t: What is the antonym of the word "impulsively" as used in the passage?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Impulsively" का मतलब है बिना सोचे-समझे झटपट कोई काम करना। इसका विलोम (Antonym) होगा "Carefully" (सोच-समझकर या सावधानी से)। Hindi Meaning: बिना सोचे-समझे (Impulsively).

t: According to the passage, how can schools help youngsters maintain a healthy diet?
o: By providing access to healthy meals and nutrition education
By allowing students to eat whatever they want
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में साफ़ लिखा है: "by providing access to nutritious meals and educating young people about the consequences of poor dietary choices."

p: Grounded Theory (also known as Grounded Research) is a method of qualitative research that uses an inductive approach to develop theories based on empirical data, making it closely connected to the principles of inductive reasoning in research. Researchers do not start with a theory or idea beforehand. Instead, they analyse the data to find patterns and themes. These patterns and themes are then used to create a theory that explains the social process or situation being studied.

Imagine researchers want to understand how people cope with job loss. They start by interviewing several individuals who recently lost their jobs, asking open-ended questions about their experiences and emotions. As they analyse these interviews, patterns begin to emerge- such as strategies people use to find new employment, emotional responses like stress or resilience, and changes in personal relationships. From these patterns, the researchers develop theories about the different ways individuals cope with job loss. These theories are grounded in the actual experiences and stories shared by the participants, providing a rich and detailed understanding of this aspect of human behavior.

t: What makes Grounded Theory stand apart from other research methods?
o: It begins with a fixed theoretical framework and tests it against collected data, leaving little room for new insights
It mainly uses surveys and statistics to check if earlier ideas about social behavior are correct
It emphasizes the application of pre-established models to interpret social processes, rather than constructing new models based on observational data
It starts without any preconceived theory, allowing patterns and themes from real-world data to shape the final theory
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: ग्राउंडेड थ्योरी बिना पहले से तय सिद्धांत के शुरू होती है और वास्तविक डेटा के पैटर्न व थीम से सिद्धांत बनाती है।

t: Why do we call Grounded Theory an inductive approach?
o: This approach begins with established theories, using them to generate predictions that are subsequently tested through systematic experimentation.
This approach starts with a hypothesis and employs organized data collection methods to determine whether the hypothesis is supported or refuted.
It applies general principles through deductive reasoning to interpret and explain particular cases encountered in the research.
Grounded Theory develops broader theoretical insights by systematically analyzing specific observations and detailed data, allowing theories to emerge from the data itself.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: इसे inductive कहते हैं क्योंकि यह विशिष्ट अवलोकनों के विश्लेषण से व्यापक सिद्धांत निकालती है, जबकि deductive में सामान्य सिद्धांत से विशेष की ओर जाते हैं।

t: Imagine a group of researchers wants to understand how individuals deal with losing their jobs. According to Grounded Theory, which of the following best describes how they would approach this study?
o: They would start by using an established psychological theory about stress and resilience to interpret what people share in their interviews.
They would design a structured questionnaire informed by previous research and use statistical methods to confirm patterns that have already been identified in coping with job loss.
They would focus on analyzing existing studies and literature to validate well-known models of how people adjust to unemployment.

They would begin by conducting open-ended interviews, carefully looking for common themes such as emotional reactions and coping strategies, and then develop a theory directly from these observations.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: ग्राउंडेड थ्योरी के अनुसार शोधकर्ता खुले प्रश्नों वाले साक्षात्कार करेंगे, साझा थीम (भावनाएँ, रणनीतियाँ) खोजेंगे और फिर उन्हीं से सिद्धांत बनाएँगे।

t: Select the statement that best expresses the essence of Grounded Theory:
o: Uses quantitative methods to confirm known theories
Applies general concepts to specific cases for validation
Develops new theories from qualitative, real-world data
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: ग्राउंडेड थ्योरी का सार: गुणात्मक (qualitative), वास्तविक-जीवन डेटा से नया सिद्धांत विकसित करना, न कि पहले से ज्ञात सिद्धांत की पुष्टि करना।

t: What are the primary reasons researchers choose Grounded Theory as a methodology in social studies?
o: Grounded Theory allows researchers to quickly confirm established theories without collecting much new data.
Grounded Theory is chosen primarily for its exclusive focus on quantitative data and its emphasis on achieving statistically generalizable results.
Researchers prefer Grounded Theory because it limits interpretation by relying on strict, pre-set categories when coding data.
Researchers value Grounded Theory because it offers flexibility to explore complex human behaviors and develop theories that are grounded in real-life experiences.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: शोधकर्ता इसे इसलिए चुनते हैं क्योंकि यह जटिल मानव व्यवहार को खोजने का लचीलापन देती है और सिद्धांत वास्तविक अनुभवों में निहित (grounded) होते हैं।

p: In contemporary discourse, "free will" is often celebrated as the cornerstone of individual autonomy and democratic agency. Yet, a deeper examination reveals that this perceived freedom may be more constructed than authentic. Modern society, while outwardly championing liberty, subtly engineers conformity through systems of social conditioning, digital surveillance, and algorithmic manipulation. The choices we make — what to wear, what to consume, even what to believe — are frequently shaped less by volition than by invisible frameworks of control. Consumer behavior is a telling example. Market forces, armed with behavioral data and predictive analytics, sculpt preferences before individuals are even conscious of them. Personalization engines masquerade as facilitators of choice, but in reality, they nudge individuals toward decisions already engineered to optimize corporate profit. Similarly, social media platforms curate information ecosystems that reinforce existing biases, creating cognitive echo chambers that masquerade as informed choice. Even political decisions — arguably the most significant expression of agency — are susceptible to manipulation. Campaign strategies leveraging psychographic profiling can influence voting behavior by exploiting psychological vulnerabilities rather than rational deliberation. The illusion of participation, thus, replaces genuine engagement. Moreover, societal norms, instilled through education, media, and cultural traditions, define the boundaries within which 'freedom' operates. A person may "choose" a career path, but that choice is often filtered through expectations shaped by socioeconomic class, geography, and familial pressures. What appears voluntary is often a conditioned response disguised as self-determination. To be clear, this is not an argument for fatalism, but rather a call for awareness. Recognizing the architecture that underpins our choices is the first step toward reclaiming autonomy. True agency, therefore, is not the absence of influence but the conscious interrogation of it. Without such reflection, free will in modern society may remain a comforting mirage rather than an existential reality.

t: What is the central argument of the passage?
o: Free will is incompatible with democracy
True freedom requires interrogation of influences
Modern society gives full autonomy to individuals
Autonomy is best achieved through capitalism
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक का मुख्य तर्क है कि हमारी पसंद हमारी नहीं बल्कि बाज़ार की है। असली आज़ादी के लिए हमें यह सोचना पड़ेगा कि हम जो कर रहे हैं वह क्यों कर रहे हैं ("True agency... is the conscious interrogation of it.")।

t: What is meant by "cognitive echo chambers"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Cognitive echo chambers" वह स्थिति है जहाँ सोशल मीडिया हमें सिर्फ वही दिखाता है जो हम देखना चाहते हैं, जिससे हमारे पुराने विचार (existing biases) और पक्के हो जाते हैं। Hindi Meaning: ऐसी जगह जहाँ सिर्फ अपने ही विचारों की गूँज सुनाई दे.

t: According to the passage, how do personalization algorithms affect consumer choice?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "they nudge individuals toward decisions already engineered to optimize corporate profit." (वे चुपके से हमारी पसंद को बदल देते हैं ताकि कंपनियों को फायदा हो)।

t: Why does the author mention career choices in the context of free will?
o: To show how education leads to autonomy
To highlight the irrelevance of family
To illustrate the illusion of self-determination shaped by societal filters
To argue that class no longer matters
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: करियर के उदाहरण से लेखक यह समझा रहा है कि जिसे हम अपनी "पसंद" (self-determination) मानते हैं, वह वास्तव में हमारे परिवार, समाज और क्लास के दबावों (societal filters) से तय होती है।

t: What tone best describes the author's perspective?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक 'फ्री विल' (Free Will) की आधुनिक धारणा की 'आलोचना' (critical) करता है और पाठकों को इस पर गहराई से 'विचार' (reflective) करने के लिए प्रेरित करता है।

p: In modern households, electrical devices are as common as furniture. From refrigerators and washing machines to smart televisions and microwave ovens, these appliances have transformed domestic life. However, their increasing presence has also heightened the risks, particularly for children, whose natural curiosity often overrides caution. Electrical devices operate on currents that can cause severe injury or even death if mishandled. Young children, unaware of these dangers, may insert fingers or objects into sockets, tug at dangling cords, or attempt to open appliance panels. Such actions can result in shocks, burns, or mechanical harm. Even low voltage devices, if defective or poorly maintained, can be hazardous. The responsibility for preventing accidents rests largely with adults. Installing socket covers, keeping cords out of reach, and unplugging appliances when not in use are basic precautions. More advanced measures include using Residual Current Devices (RCDs), which automatically cut off power during faults, and ensuring all wiring complies with safety standards. Regular inspection of devices is equally critical, as frayed wires or exposed components can turn everyday items into hidden threats. Education plays a vital role. Teaching children the "look, don't touch" rule, explaining the dangers of electricity in age-appropriate terms, and supervising them around devices are all effective strategies. Safety is not merely a matter of physical barriers but also of fostering awareness. Ultimately, a home equipped with electrical conveniences need not be a danger zone. Through vigilant supervision, proper maintenance, and informed habits, families can enjoy technology while safeguarding their youngest members.

t: "Families can enjoy technology while safeguarding their youngest members." Rewrite the above sentence in passive voice.
o: Technology can be enjoyed by families while their youngest members are safeguarded.
Technology is enjoyed by families while safeguarding their youngest members.
Technology will be enjoyed by families while their youngest members safeguard them.
Technology has been enjoyed by families while safeguarding their youngest members.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य में दो हिस्से बदलने हैं। "Families can enjoy technology" → "Technology can be enjoyed by families" (modal passive)। "safeguarding their youngest members" → "while their youngest members are safeguarded"। Option (a) दोनों हिस्सों को सही बदलता है, जबकि (b) और (c) सिर्फ़ आंशिक बदलाव करते हैं। उत्तर (a)।

t: "Education plays a vital role." Change the above sentence into an interrogative sentence without changing its meaning.
o: Does education play a vital role?
Is education playing a vital role?
Has education played a vital role?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: मूल वाक्य Simple Present ("plays") में है। Simple Present का Yes/No प्रश्न बनाने के लिए सामने "does" लगाते हैं और verb अपने base form में लौट आती है: "Does education play ...?" Option (c) इसे Present Continuous और (d) Present Perfect बना देता है, जिससे tense बदल जाता है। Trick: Does + subject + V1। उत्तर (b)।

t: Which of the following is the correct collocation used in the passage to describe constant and careful observation?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज के आख़िरी paragraph में ठीक यही phrase "vigilant supervision" आया है, जिसमें "vigilant" (सतर्क) और "supervision" (निगरानी) जुड़े हैं। यह लगातार और सावधान निगरानी बताने वाला collocation है जो सीधे पैसेज से लिया गया है। उत्तर (c) Vigilant supervision।

t: Which word from the passage means "hidden danger"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज "hidden threats" का प्रयोग करता है, यह बताने के लिए कि टूटे तार या खुले हिस्से रोज़मर्रा की चीज़ों को ख़तरे का स्रोत बना देते हैं। संदर्भ में "Threat" यानी छिपा हुआ ख़तरा जिससे नुकसान हो सकता है। "Hazard" भी क़रीब है, पर पैसेज में सटीक शब्द "threats" आया है। उत्तर (b) Threat। Hindi Meaning: ख़तरा।

t: According to the passage, what is the primary reason children are at risk around electrical devices?
o: They are often unsupervised at home.
Their curiosity can lead them to unsafe interactions.
They like playing with toys near appliances.
They are physically weaker than adults.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज बच्चों के जोखिम की जड़ साफ़ बताता है: "their natural curiosity often overrides caution." बच्चों की खोजने की स्वाभाविक प्रवृत्ति उन्हें सॉकेट में चीज़ें डालने, तार खींचने या पैनल खोलने जैसी असुरक्षित हरकतों की ओर ले जाती है। उत्तर (b)।

p: "The explanation of a work is always sought in the man or woman who produced it, as if it were always, in the end, through the voice of a single person that literature spoke: through the voice of a single person and the imprints of his or her passions. The image of literature that we seek to sustain is tyrannically centered on the author, his life, his history, and his intentions. But to give a text an Author is to impose a limit on that text, to furnish it with a final signified, to close the writing. Such a conception is born of the rationalist and capitalist ideologies that have placed the individual at the center of history, emphasizing his authority and coherence. Yet, in reality, writing is a destruction of every voice, of every point of origin. Writing begins at the moment the Author is set aside, and language speaks—not the Author. To refuse the Author is not to refuse meaning, but to refuse the tyranny of a single, authoritative meaning. The text, instead, becomes a space of multiple interpretations, where meaning is neither fixed nor final. The unity of a text is not located in its origin but in its destination; it is the reader, not the Author, who gives meaning to a text. This radical displacement shifts the power from the creator to the interpreter, from the supposed intention of the writer to the infinite play of signifiers within the text itself."

t: What is the grammatical function of the clause "that we seek to sustain"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "The image of literature that we seek to sustain..." यहाँ "that" एक Relative Pronoun है जो 'image' (Noun) के बारे में अतिरिक्त जानकारी दे रहा है। इसे Relative Clause कहते हैं।

t: Which sentence contains a correct use of the passive voice from the passage?
o: "The Author creates the meaning of the text."
"The text is furnished with a final signified."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: यह वाक्य Passive Voice में है : Subject (The text) + is + V3 (furnished) + with... बाकी सारे विकल्प Active Voice में हैं।

t: What does the word "tyrannically" most closely mean in the phrase "tyrannically centred on the author"?
o: In a cruel and absolute way
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Tyrannically" का अर्थ होता है एक तानाशाह (Tyrant) की तरह, जो क्रूर और पूर्ण सत्ता (absolute authority) का प्रयोग करता हो। Hindi Meaning: तानाशाही / क्रूर और पूर्ण तरीके से.

t: What is the best synonym for "inherent" in this sentence: "The notion of 'the Author' is a construct of cultural expectation rather than an inherent necessity of literature."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Inherent" का अर्थ होता है किसी चीज़ के अंदर स्वाभाविक (natural) रूप से मौजूद गुण, जो बाहर से न लिया गया हो। 'Natural' इसका सबसे सटीक समानार्थी है। 'Acquired' (प्राप्त किया हुआ) इसका विलोम है। Hindi Meaning: जन्मजात / स्वाभाविक / प्राकृतिक.

t: According to Barthes, what happens when we remove the Author from our understanding of literature?
o: The text gains the freedom to mean different things.
The author's life becomes even more important.
Interpretation is limited to historical context.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक कहता है कि "To refuse the Author... the text becomes a space of multiple interpretations." (लेखक को हटाने पर पाठ के कई अर्थ निकल सकते हैं , यानी पाठ को अलग-अलग अर्थ देने की आज़ादी मिल जाती है)।

p: Medical waste management is one of the most important yet often overlooked aspects of healthcare. Hospitals, clinics, and laboratories generate large amounts of waste every day, including used syringes, bandages, gloves, and other materials that may be contaminated. If not handled and disposed of properly, this waste can pose serious risks to human health and the environment. Proper medical waste management involves separating, treating, and safely disposing of different types of waste. Many healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines to ensure that hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste. Incineration, chemical treatment, and secure landfills are some common methods used to manage medical waste. However, poor management and lack of awareness still lead to unsafe disposal practices in some places. Experts believe that training healthcare workers, strict enforcement of rules, and public awareness are essential to improving medical waste management and protecting communities from potential harm.

t: Identify the voice (active or passive) and the tense of the verb in the sentence: "Many healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines to ensure that hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: मुख्य क्लॉज़ है "Many healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines". यहाँ 'institutions' (Subject) खुद काम कर रहा है (Active Voice) और क्रिया (follow) Simple Present Tense (V1) में है।

t: Identify the part of speech of the word "properly" in the sentence: "If not handled and disposed of properly, this waste can pose serious risks to human health and the environment."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Properly" शब्द यह बता रहा है कि कचरे को 'कैसे' (how) हैंडल और डिस्पोज़ (verb) किया जाना चाहिए। जो शब्द क्रिया (verb) की विशेषता बताता है, वह Adverb (क्रिया-विशेषण) होता है।

t: The word "contaminated" means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: मेडिकल साइंस में 'Contaminated' का अर्थ होता है किसी चीज़ का जीवाणुओं या रसायनों के संपर्क में आकर 'दूषित या संक्रमित' (infected/impure) हो जाना।

t: The word "hazardous" means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Hazardous" का अर्थ होता है 'खतरनाक या नुकसानदायक'।

t: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Medical waste management is essential to protect health and environment
Hospitals can mix all waste together
Incineration is the only method of disposal
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पूरा पैसेज इसी बात पर ज़ोर देता है कि मेडिकल वेस्ट का सही तरीके से निपटारा करना इंसान और पर्यावरण दोनों के लिए बेहद ज़रूरी है।

p: The inheritance of culture is rarely obvious. What we call tradition is often just repetition with reverence, and what we call structure is more often sediment-settled behaviors shaped by forgotten motives. No individual wakes up conscious of the script they perform daily: the deference coded into language, the hierarchy in who speaks and who listens, the legitimacy given to one dialect over another. These scripts are learned by doing, not by knowing. Structures do not enforce themselves through law alone; they linger in weddings, gestures, floor plans, and silence. The most enduring hierarchies don't shout they whisper, hiding in rituals too familiar to question. When efforts are made to 'preserve culture,' they often freeze one version of the past, assuming it pure and unchanging. However, culture never stood still. It changes, not by denial, but by negotiation. To honor a legacy is not to protect its shape, but to confront what it excludes. If history is architecture, then culture is weather - it reshapes even stone, slowly, insistently. A society unwilling to interrogate its inherited rhythms is not preserving culture - it is embalming it.

t: What is the author's main claim about cultural inheritance?
q.sr: [SSC Stenographer Grade C & D Examination, 2026, 15 sep 2026, Shift- 1]
o: It is taught consciously through education
It is reinforced by formal institutions only
It is practiced unconsciously through daily behavior
It is dictated directly by written tradition
q.e: The author strongly claims that individuals unconsciously perform cultural scripts daily, explicitly stating that "These scripts are learned by doing, not by knowing" and naturally hide in familiar everyday rituals and mundane gestures.

t: What metaphor best captures the author's contrast between history and culture?
o: Culture is a mirror; history is its shadow
History is architecture; culture is weather
Culture is a seed; history is the soil
History is fiction; culture is myth
q.e: The passage vividly utilizes a profound metaphor to draw a sharp contrast, explicitly writing verbatim: "If history is architecture, then culture is weather - it reshapes even stone, slowly, insistently."

t: According to the passage, what is a problem with efforts to 'preserve culture'?
o: They freeze culture as static and exclude others
q.e: The text powerfully critiques standard preservation efforts, noting that "they often freeze one version of the past, assuming it pure and unchanging," which fundamentally fails to deeply confront "what it excludes."

t: What tone does the author use toward cultural rituals?
q.e: The author clearly respects the profound depth of cultural legacy (calling for us to truly "honor" it) but insists heavily on constantly questioning and aggressively interrogating its underlying structures, making it highly affectionate yet deeply interrogative.

t: What does the passage suggest about truly honoring a legacy?
o: Ask what or whom it excludes
q.e: The text explicitly defines true respect for heritage, fiercely stating: "To honor a legacy is not to protect its shape, but to confront what it excludes." This necessitates asking hard questions about marginalized exclusions.

p: Everyday life studies began after industrialization and aim to reveal and interpret the routines that shape our daily experiences. This field uses anthropological analysis, which was once mainly used for non-Western societies, to look at modern Western life. The main goal is to study familiar behaviours that often go unnoticed because they are so ordinary. Artists and social theorists in this area document and examine overlooked parts of daily life, like sleeping, walking, eating, working, recreation, self-care, and interactions with others. Everyday life studies are sometimes called the science of the 'small.' They focus on micro-moments and micro-actions, such as turning a street corner, stirring a pot, or feeding a baby. Although these actions are often seen within larger social structures, the small, everyday actions are not seen as important events and usually do not appear in historical records. They are called 'everyday' not just because they are ordinary, but also because they happen daily or even several times a day. Whether connected to our body's natural rhythms or to wage work, these small actions are defined by how often they repeat. Scholars who study everyday life, especially in modern times, have different views on the political meaning of daily routines. Some connect this repetition to the mechanisation and alienation found in capitalist labour.

t: Everyday life studies apply anthropological methods to the ordinary routines of modern societies.
o: These studies focus on the small, unnoticed actions that shape our experiences.
They mainly examine major political events that change a country's history.
They try to take the place of sociology by focusing only on economic systems.
They study only non-Western rituals without engaging with Western contexts.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: Everyday life studies आधुनिक समाजों की सामान्य दिनचर्या पर मानवशास्त्रीय विधियाँ लागू करती हैं और छोटे, अनदेखे कार्यों पर ध्यान देती हैं।

t: The field is sometimes called the "science of the small" because it attends closely to repeated micro-moments.
o: It concentrates on rare behaviors that appear only in unusual situations.
It highlights tiny, repeated actions like stirring food or turning a corner.
It documents historic events that already dominate written archives.
It limits itself to specialized gestures requiring expert training.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: इसे 'science of the small' इसलिए कहते हैं क्योंकि यह बार-बार दोहराए जाने वाले सूक्ष्म कार्यों (जैसे बर्तन चलाना, मोड़ मुड़ना) पर ध्यान देती है।

t: What are the primary reasons that everyday routines are infrequently documented in historical records?
o: Everyday habits usually occur in personal or private spaces, which makes them less visible and therefore less likely to be recorded.
Governments often place limits on what is shared about private, domestic life.
They are not regarded as crucial events that merit documentation.
These daily routines may sometimes conflict with the prevailing political narratives of the period, so they tend to be left out of official histories.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: ये छोटे रोज़मर्रा के कार्य महत्वपूर्ण घटना नहीं माने जाते, इसलिए ऐतिहासिक अभिलेखों में प्रायः दर्ज नहीं होते।

t: What makes an action "every day," according to the passage?
o: Its uniqueness and rarity within a person's daily experiences.
Its performance is only during public rituals or official ceremonies.
Its requirement for specialized cultural or professional training.
Its frequent repetition is tied to bodily rhythms or forms of wage labour.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: कार्य 'everyday' इसलिए है कि यह रोज़ या दिन में कई बार दोहराया जाता है, जो शरीर की लय या वेतन-श्रम से जुड़ा होता है।

t: In what ways do scholars interpret the political significance of daily repetition?
o: Others regard daily repetition as politically neutral and disconnected from broader social or economic structures.
Some scholars contend that repetition enables complete independence from economic forces.
Some scholars associate daily repetition with mechanization and alienation characteristic of capitalist systems.
Others see daily repetition as a form of resistance to all types of labor discipline.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज के अंतिम वाक्य: कुछ विद्वान इस दोहराव को पूँजीवादी श्रम के यंत्रीकरण और अलगाव (alienation) से जोड़ते हैं।

p: Art, in its manifold forms — visual, performative, literary, and auditory — constitutes a domain that transcends utilitarian function and enters the realm of the symbolic, the affective, and the transformative. Its significance within society cannot be reduced to decoration or diversion; rather, it operates as a mode of critical reflection, a vessel of collective memory, and a catalyst for socio-cultural evolution. At its core, art interrogates the contours of reality by reframing perception. Whether through the destabilizing surrealism of a Dali canvas or the dissonant harmonies of avant-garde music, art dislodges the observer from complacency and compels re-engagement with the world. It is in this function that art becomes not only an aesthetic but an epistemological act — challenging dominant paradigms and opening discursive space for marginalized narratives. Historically, art has served as an archive of civilizations, encoding within its mediums the aspirations, anxieties, and ideologies of its epoch. From the sacred iconography of temple frescoes to the protest murals adorning urban decay, art becomes a text through which power, resistance, and identity are simultaneously contested and constituted. This historical embeddedness renders art indispensable to understanding not only what a society creates but what it values and fears. In modern democracies, the role of art assumes a distinctly political dimension. Art enables dissent when speech is suppressed, and engenders empathy where rational argument fails. Satire, documentary film, and performance art often articulate the unspeakable, using metaphor and allusion to subvert censure. Yet this potential also renders art vulnerable — to censorship, commodification, and ideological co-option. When stripped of autonomy, art may devolve into propaganda or elitist ornamentation — devoid of critical function. The sociological function of art extends to its capacity to cultivate communal belonging and individual introspection simultaneously.

Participatory forms of art — street theatre, public installations, folk traditions — dissolve the binaries of creator and audience, democratizing aesthetic engagement. Meanwhile, solitary encounters with a painting or a poem can occasion personal revelation, catharsis, or ethical inquiry. However, in the algorithmic age, where virality and visibility often dictate cultural value, art faces unprecedented commodification. The aesthetic is frequently reduced to a spectacle optimized for consumption, divorced from nuance, complexity, or transgression. The challenge, therefore, is to preserve the sanctity of artistic integrity in the face of market and media pressures that threaten to flatten it into banality. Ultimately, the role of art in society is neither static nor monolithic. It is a dialectical force — at once reflective and projective, disruptive and redemptive. To safeguard art is to safeguard the capacity of humanity to feel, to question, and to reimagine.

t: What is implied by describing art as an "epistemological act" in the passage?
o: Art is a method of acquiring and challenging knowledge structures.
Art serves as mere historical documentation.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Epistemology ज्ञान (knowledge) का अध्ययन है। कला को "epistemological act" कहने का अर्थ है कि कला केवल सुंदर नहीं दिखती, बल्कि यह समाज के बने-बनाए 'ज्ञान के ढांचों' (dominant paradigms) को चुनौती भी देती है।

t: The phrase "commodification of art" in the passage most nearly refers to:
o: Art being preserved in national archives.
Art being transformed into a consumer product stripped of its critical power.
Art being used exclusively for educational purposes.
Art becoming a tool for political awareness.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Commodification" (व्यवसायीकरण) का मतलब है कला को महज़ बिकने वाला एक 'उत्पाद' (consumer product) बना देना, जिससे उसकी गहराई और आलोचनात्मक शक्ति (critical function) खत्म हो जाती है।

t: According to the passage, how does art function in politically repressive environments?
o: It reinforces state propaganda through images.
It channels dissent and expresses unspeakable truths.
It remains confined to academic circles.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: जब बोलने पर पाबंदी होती है, तो कला "enables dissent when speech is suppressed" (विरोध दर्ज कराती है) और उन बातों को रूपकों (metaphor) के ज़रिए कहती है जो सीधे नहीं कही जा सकतीं।

t: Which of the following best explains the dialectical nature of art as per the last paragraph?
o: Art is always destructive and marginal.
Art evolves through opposing forces of creation and criticism.
Art functions only within elite institutions.
Art is limited to reflecting the past.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Dialectical' (द्वंद्वात्मक) का अर्थ है दो विरोधी चीज़ों (जैसे reflective and projective, disruptive and redemptive) के बीच का टकराव या उनका साथ चलना, जिससे कला विकसित होती है।

t: What is the closest meaning of the word "banality" as used in the sentence: "...threaten to flatten it into banality"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Banality' का अर्थ होता है किसी चीज़ का इतना आम या साधारण हो जाना कि उसमें कोई गहराई या नयापन न रहे (तुच्छता)। इसका सबसे करीबी अर्थ 'Triviality' (तुच्छता) है।

p: Freedom of speech is a cornerstone of democratic societies, allowing individuals to express ideas, question authority, and promote change. However, in the digital world, this right encounters complex challenges. Social media platforms have become arenas where opinions can be voiced instantly-but also where hate speech, misinformation, and cyberbullying thrive. Balancing the right to speak freely with the responsibility to prevent harm is now a pressing debate. Should platforms censor harmful content, or would that violate freedom? While some argue that regulation is essential to protect vulnerable groups, others fear it might lead to suppression of dissent. The problem deepens when private companies-not elected bodies-decide what speech is allowed or banned. Striking the right balance requires thoughtful policies, digital literacy, and legal frameworks rooted in both human rights and public safety.
